title: Hearty One Pot Polish Dill Pickle Soup with Sausage
summary: This comforting one-pot pickle soup offers a vibrant balance of sour, savory, and creamy textures in every bowl. Tangy grated dill pickles simmer in a rich poultry stock alongside tender potatoes, carrots, and smoky kielbasa sausage. Sauteed onions, garlic, and leeks establish a fragrant aromatic foundation that elevates the tangy broth. A touch of sour cream and flour creates a smooth, velvety finish without overwhelming the distinctive tart character of fermented pickles. Fresh dill, black pepper, and sour pickle brine added at the finish bring a bright, energizing aroma to the hot pot. Diced root vegetables absorb the savory broth while cooking, yielding a hearty stew-like consistency ideal for cool weather dining. Everything cooks sequentially in a single heavy Dutch oven, making prep and cleanup effortlessly simple. Rich, satisfying, and full of traditional Polish comfort, this soup is best enjoyed hot with crusty rye bread.

steps.step: Place large Dutch oven pot onto center stove burner over medium heat setting.
Melt butter and vegetable oil in hot pot until liquid bubbles gently on bottom.
Add sliced kielbasa sausage rounds to pot and sear for four minutes until brown.
Transfer seared sausage pieces to clean side plate using slotted spoon.
Add diced yellow onion and sliced shallots to rendered fat remaining in pot.
Sauté onions and shallots for four minutes until soft and translucent golden hue.
Add sliced leek rings and minced garlic to pot, stirring for two minutes until soft.
Pour chicken broth into pot, stirring bottom with spoon to release caramelized bits.
Add bay leaves, allspice berries, and caraway seeds into warm broth in pot.
Add dried thyme, marjoram, and paprika to broth, stirring well to combine spices.
Increase heat under pot to high and bring broth mixture to active rolling boil.
Reduce heat to medium low and simmer broth for ten minutes to develop rich base.
Skim any floating excess foam off broth surface using broad metal spoon.
Taste broth base and add one teaspoon salt and black pepper according to taste.
Keep broth at gentle steady simmer while processing root vegetables on board.
Verify onion and garlic pieces have softened completely into simmering broth.
Check that all spice aromatics are evenly distributed throughout liquid base.
Prepare diced potatoes, carrots, and parsnips for pot addition in next step.
Keep seared sausage plate covered loosely near stove for reintroduction later.
Confirm Dutch oven liquid level is sufficient for cooking dense root vegetables.
Maintain steady medium low burner flame under Dutch oven during ingredient prep.
Peel Yukon Gold potatoes and cut into uniform half inch dice for even pot cooking.
Peel carrots and slice into neat quarter inch round coins on cutting board.
Peel parsnip and celery root, cutting both into half inch dice matching potatoes.
Slice celery stalks into thin crescent pieces and add to diced root vegetable bowl.
Grate dill pickles using coarse side of box grater into medium glass bowl.
Measure out dill pickle brine liquid from jar, ensuring no pickle seeds remain.
Melt clarified butter in small side skillet over medium heat for sautéing pickles.
Add grated dill pickles to side skillet and sauté for five minutes to soften texture.
Sautéing grated pickles tames raw sharp edge and concentrates warm sour flavors.
Add sugar and mustard seeds to sautéed pickles in side skillet, stirring once.
Remove side skillet from heat and let grated pickles rest while vegetables boil.
Add diced potatoes, carrots, parsnips, and celery root into simmering pot broth.
Add diced celery pieces into pot, pushing vegetables below broth liquid level.
Cover Dutch oven with lid and cook vegetables for fifteen minutes until tender.
Check potato tenderness by piercing center piece gently with tip of paring knife.
Ensure carrots and parsnips are soft through center before adding sour pickles.
Keep stove flame steady so vegetables cook uniformly without breaking apart.
Prepare sour cream temper mixture while root vegetables complete cooking phase.
Verify all root vegetable pieces are fully submerged in simmering broth.
Maintain organized work space by clearing vegetable peelings into trash bin.
Return seared kielbasa sausage rounds to Dutch oven containing soft vegetables.
Stir sautéed grated pickles into soup pot, distributing pickles evenly throughout.
Pour in measured dill pickle brine liquid and extra pickle juice into pot.
Stir soup pot thoroughly to combine sour pickle brine with savory stock broth.
Add garlic powder, onion powder, and celery salt into pot to deepen seasonings.
Add ground nutmeg and white pepper to soup pot, stirring broth from bottom up.
Simmer soup mixture uncovered for ten minutes to let pickle flavor infuse pot.
Check that sausage slices are hot through and render additional smoky flavor.
Taste broth to evaluate balance between sour pickle acidity and savory sausage.
Add white wine vinegar and lemon juice if stronger sour note is desired in soup.
Whisk sour cream, heavy cream, and all purpose flour in small mixing bowl.
Ladle one cup of hot soup broth into cream mixture while whisking constantly.
Tempering cream mixture prevents curdling when introduced into hot acidic soup.
Whisk tempered cream mixture until completely smooth without any flour lumps.
Slowly pour tempered cream mixture into simmering soup pot while stirring gently.
Stir soup continuously for three minutes as flour thickens broth into silky texture.
Reduce burner heat to low to prevent soup from boiling once cream is added.
Check consistency of soup broth; it should coat back of wooden spoon lightly.
Stir prepared horseradish into creamy broth for subtle sharp background kick.
Keep pot at gentle simmer for five minutes to complete flavor integration step.
Chop fresh dill finely, discarding coarse bottom stems on cutting board.
Chop fresh parsley and fresh chives finely for final herbal soup garnishes.
Stir half of chopped fresh dill into simmering pickle soup pot gently.
Stir chopped parsley into pot, holding remaining dill and chives for bowls.
Fish out bay leaves and allspice berries from soup pot using spoon and discard.
Season soup with sea salt flakes and black pepper after tasting thick broth.
Add cayenne pepper for slight warm finish that complements sour pickle notes.
Simmer soup on low heat for final three minutes to settle all combined flavors.
Turn off stove burner flame and let Dutch oven sit on warm burner two minutes.
Inspect soup surface to confirm creamy homogeneous texture throughout pot.
Slice fresh rye bread into thick slices and place on bread board for table.
Warm soup bowls by rinsing with hot water and drying with clean towel.
Ladle generous portion of pickle soup into each warmed soup bowl carefully.
Ensure each serving bowl receives balanced mix of sausage, potatoes, and pickles.
Garnish center of each soup bowl with remaining fresh dill and chives.
Dust top of each bowl lightly with additional black pepper and paprika.
Drizzle few drops of olive oil on surface of each bowl for glossy finish.
Arrange buttered rye bread slices beside each soup bowl on dining table.
Provide extra sour cream at table for guests who prefer extra rich soup.
Carry hot soup bowls to table immediately for ideal cozy dining enjoyment.
Verify overall acidity levels in soup bowls match traditional sour Polish profile.
Offer extra pickle brine at table for guests seeking extreme tangy sharpness.
Refrigerate any leftover soup in covered glass container after cooling completely.
Note that pickle soup tastes even more flavorful when reheated next day.
To reheat leftovers, warm gently over low heat on stove without boiling soup.
Add splash of stock or water if soup thickens excessively in refrigerator overnight.
Check that potatoes remain whole and soft without dissolving into broth base.
Wipe Dutch oven rim clean before storing pot in refrigerator or serving table.
Enjoy authentic one pot Polish dill pickle soup with warm rye bread slices.
Clean cooking utensils and cutting boards while soup pot settles after meal.
Serve soup as main course during cold weather family dinners and gatherings.
Keep extra fresh dill herbs wrapped in damp towel for future soup batches.
Confirm all diners enjoy contrast of smoky sausage with sour pickle broth.
Store remaining rye bread wrapped tightly in paper bag to preserve crustiness.
Check that pickle brine salinity was well balanced by potatoes during cook.
Use remaining sour cream within three days for optimal fresh dairy flavor.
Record any preferred spice adjustments in recipe notebook for future cooks.
Keep extra black pepper grinder handy at table for personal seasoning.
Enjoy easy cleanup provided by cooking entire recipe inside one pot.
Conclude Polish dinner service successfully with satisfied dinner guests.
